text:
incident-bot: AUTO-PAGE fired for latency.p99 > 1000ms for route /v2/generate (model=redwood-v2-prod) in prod-east :rotating_light:
pagerduty: PagerDuty incident PD-8732 triggered — urgent (page sent to oncall)
pagerduty: Details: metric=latency.p99 threshold=1000ms current=1560ms window=5m
matt_oncall: acked — taking this. I'm oncall for the next 30m. Starting triage.
sarah_ux: @matt_oncall heads-up: support flagged a few customers seeing timeouts. Not full outage but degraded UX.
raj_sre: looking at autoscaler and KV cache metrics now. tagging logs. Can we confirm if this is single-model hotpath or cluster-wide?
matt_oncall: initial dash shows spike concentrated on pods serving redwood-v2-prod (hot path). p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 1560ms. Errors not spiking.
jing_ml: recent rollout of a new attention-kernel patch yesterday? Could be kernel regression or a bad batch pattern. I will check model release tags.
raj_sre: metrics: GPU mem pressure + queue depth high on nodes eu-prod-east-2. KV cache write miss rate up 8x. Looks like prefix cache thrash. Suggest immediate mitigations: 1) temporary disable continuous batching for this model 2) scale up dedicated pool by +2 nodes 3) route traffic to redwood-v2-quant fallback if latency persists.
matt_oncall: agreed. Executing mitigations in order.
raj_sre: Command I ran: ```
# disable batching on model config
redwoodctl config set redwood-v2-prod batching.enabled false --env=prod-east
# scale up pool
redwoodctl cluster scale pool prod-east-pool --add 2 --reason "p99 latency surge"
```
sarah_ux: FYI I posted a short status to #general-customer-notify: "We’re seeing elevated generation latency for a subset of requests in prod-east; engineers are mitigating. No data loss expected."
pagerduty: PD note: incident acknowledged by matt_oncall at 12:10 UTC. Escalation policy: will auto-escalate in 10m if not resolved.
jing_ml: checked model release: rollback NOT applied. I’m running a quick per-shard profiler to verify attention kernel perf. If it’s a kernel regression, we should revert.
raj_sre: After disabling batching, p99 dropped from ~1560ms -> ~720ms in 2m. Good improvement but still above 1000ms earlier, trending down.
matt_oncall: Noted. Putting autopager on snooze for 15m while we stabilize to avoid noisy re-page: `incident-bot: autopager snooze 15m by matt_oncall`
incident-bot: Auto-pager snoozed for 15 minutes by matt_oncall.
raj_sre: Next step: KV cache flush to clear thrash and warm common prefixes. Command: ```
redwoodctl kvcache flush --model redwood-v2-prod --region prod-east
```
raj_sre: After flush p99 -> 430ms, p95 -> 190ms. Nice.
sarah_ux: Support: customers reporting improved response times. No new timeouts.
jing_ml: Profiler results show increased kernel L2 misses on specific GPU type but not universal. I’ll roll back the kernel patch on the small canary group; if that fixes, schedule full revert.
matt_oncall: I'll keep monitoring. If p99 holds < 900ms for 10m, we can start closing. Handing off to @raj_sre for continued watch and H1 runbook tasks. I'm available if it re-escalates.
raj_sre: Taking over monitoring. Documenting mitigation steps in incident ticket INC-2026-345. Assigning postmortem to jing_ml and raj_sre.
pagerduty: PD update: escalation cancelled at 12:25 UTC; incident status: acknowledged -> under mitigation.
incident-bot: Note: created temporary routing rule to divert 20% traffic to redwood-v2-quant in prod-east as precaution. Rule id=rt-6821.
raj_sre: scaling down backlog consumers and disabling long-tail batching helped latency. Plan: 1) keep batching disabled for model for 1h 2) schedule controlled canary rollback of kernel at 13:00 UTC 3) add a KV cache LRU tuning ticket.
sarah_ux: internal comms: ramping messaging to impacted customers done. No legal/SEC concerns.
jing_ml: will patch canary and report perf before full revert. If canary passes, revert by 13:30.
matt_oncall: final check-in before leaving shift: p99 steady at ~380ms for 6m. Good job team. I’m handing incident to @raj_sre for post-runbook.
raj_sre: Acknowledged handoff — I will keep watch for next 45m. Closing paging flow now. Creating follow-up tasks: INC-2026-345 -> postmortem doc, kernel revert runbook, KV cache tuning RFC.
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-8732 marked resolved at 12:40 UTC by matt_oncall.
pagerduty: PD note: Incident closed. Root cause suspected: KV cache thrash exacerbated by recent kernel perf change; final determination after postmortem.
sarah_ux: Thanks all. Small retrospective: consider per-model batching toggles in console for faster mitigation. :+1:
jing_ml: Filed PR for short-term revert automation: https://git.internal/redwood/reverts/PR-421
raj_sre: Adding timelines + logs to the incident ticket. Will schedule postmortem review tomorrow 09:30 UTC.
